s: In which year did the UN General Assembly proclaim the International Day of Rural Women (Resolution 62/136)?
x: The UNGA proclaimed the day in 2007 by Resolution 62/136; it was first observed on 15 October 2008.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. UN Women was established in 2010, began operations in 2011 and has its headquarters in New York.
2. CEDAW was adopted in 1979 and came into force in 1985.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 2 is wrong: CEDAW was adopted in 1979 but came into force in 1981.

s: What is the theme of World Food Day 2026, observed on 16 October?
o: Hand in hand for better foods
x: The 2026 theme of World Food Day is "Innovate today. Nourish tomorrow."

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO)?
o: It was founded at Quebec City in 1945.
Its Director-General is Qu Dongyu of China.
World Food Day marking its founding was first observed in 1979.
x: World Food Day was first observed in 1981; 1979 was the year of the FAO Conference decision.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: WFP won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2020. IFAD dates from 1977, FAO was founded at Quebec City, and World Food Day was first observed in 1981.

s:
Consider the following statements about the International Day of the Intangible Cultural Heritage:
1. It was proclaimed at the 42nd UNESCO General Conference in November 2023.
2. It was first observed on 17 October 2024.
3. India ratified the UNESCO 2003 Convention for the Safeguarding of Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2006.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 3 is wrong: India ratified the 2003 Convention in 2005; the Convention came into force on 20 April 2006.

s: When did the UNESCO 2003 Convention for the Safeguarding of the Intangible Cultural Heritage come into force?
x: The Convention was adopted on 17 October 2003 and came into force on 20 April 2006.

s: Where was the first gathering of 17 October 1987, initiated by Joseph Wresinski, held for the eradication of poverty?
x: The first gathering was held on 17 October 1987 at Trocadero Square, Paris, initiated by Joseph Wresinski, founder of ATD Fourth World.

s:
Consider the following statements about the International Day for the Eradication of Poverty:
1. It was proclaimed by the UNGA in 1992 by Resolution 47/196.
2. In 2025 the World Bank revised the extreme poverty line to USD 2.15 per day (2021 PPP).
3. Its theme for 2026–2028 is "United for Peace and Human Rights".
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 2 is wrong: the World Bank revised the extreme poverty line to USD 3.00 per day (2021 PPP) in 2025.

s: In which year was Breast Cancer Awareness Month first launched by the American Cancer Society and the pharmaceutical division of Imperial Chemical Industries?
x: Breast Cancer Awareness Month was first launched in October 1985.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Breast Cancer Awareness Month and related facts?
o: It is also known as Pink October.
The Pink Ribbon has been its symbol since the early 1990s.
World Cancer Day on 4 February is led by WHO.
Its 2026 theme is "Every story is unique, every journey matters."
x: World Cancer Day on 4 February is led by UICC, not WHO.

s: What were the denominations of the two stamps in the souvenir sheet released by the Department of Posts for Breast Cancer Awareness Month in 2026?
x: The souvenir sheet had two stamps of ₹25 and ₹50, along with picture postcards.

s:
Consider the following statements about the commemorative postage stamps on Breast Cancer Awareness Month released in November 2026:
1. They were unveiled at Dak Bhawan, New Delhi, by DG Postal Services Manisha Sinha and Health Secretary Punya Salila Srivastava.
2. India Post, which released them, was established in 1857.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 2 is wrong: India Post was established in 1854.

s: Which organisation organises International Infection Prevention Week (19–25 October)?
x: International Infection Prevention Week is organised by APIC (Association for Professionals in Infection Control and Epidemiology).

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The theme of International Infection Prevention Week 2026 is "Generations of Infection Prevention" with the tagline "Past. Present. Protected."
2. APIC was established in 1972 and is headquartered in Arlington, Virginia, USA.
3. World AMR Awareness Week is observed from 18 to 24 October.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 3 is wrong: World AMR Awareness Week is observed from 18 to 24 November.

s: In which year did UNEP and WHO set up the Global Alliance to Eliminate Lead Paint?
x: The Global Alliance to Eliminate Lead Paint was set up by UNEP and WHO in 2011; the first Lead Poisoning Prevention Week was in 2012.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about International Lead Poisoning Prevention Week 2026?
o: It was the 14th edition, held 18–24 October 2026.
Its theme was "From Detection to Prevention".
UNEP, which supports it, has its headquarters in Nairobi.
The first such week was observed in 2011.
x: The first week was observed in 2012; 2011 is when the Global Alliance to Eliminate Lead Paint was set up.

s: What is the theme of Vigilance Awareness Week 2026 (26 October – 1 November)?
o: Corruption-free India for a Developed Nation
Culture of Integrity for Nation's Prosperity
x: The 2026 theme of Vigilance Awareness Week is "Probity for Prosperity".

s:
Assertion (A): Vigilance Awareness Week is held every year in the week around 31 October.
Reason (R): 31 October is the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, observed as National Unity Day.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: The week is held around 31 October because it is Sardar Patel's birth anniversary (National Unity Day), so R explains A.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Central Vigilance Commission (CVC):
1. It was set up in 1964 on the recommendation of the Santhanam Committee.
2. It became a statutory body through the CVC Act, 2005.
3. Vigilance Awareness Week under it has been observed since 2000.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 2 is wrong: the CVC became statutory through the CVC Act, 2003.

s: In which year did the UN General Assembly proclaim Global Media and Information Literacy Week?
x: Global MIL Week was launched in 2012 by UNESCO and partners and proclaimed by the UNGA in 2021.

s:
Consider the following statements about Global Media and Information Literacy Week:
1. It was launched in 2012 by UNESCO along with the UNESCO MIL Alliance, UNAOC and the MILID University Network.
2. In 2026 it was observed from 24 to 31 October.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: it was launched in 2012 by UNESCO and partners, and the 2026 week ran from 24 to 31 October.

s: At the UNGA's first Special Session on Disarmament in which year was UN Disarmament Week called for?
x: UN Disarmament Week was called for at the first Special Session on Disarmament in 1978 (Resolution A/RES/S-10/2).

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about UN Disarmament Week and related facts?
o: It begins on UN Day, 24 October.
It is coordinated by UNODA, headquartered in New York.
Resolution 50/72 B of 12 December 1995 encouraged public awareness about it.
India is a signatory to the NPT, which came into force in 1970.
x: The NPT came into force in 1970, but India is not a signatory.

s: Which city was the global host of World Cities Day 2026 (31 October – 2 November 2026)?
x: Fuzhou, China was the global host city of World Cities Day 2026.

s:
Consider the following statements about World Cities Day:
1. It was first observed in 2014 and was proclaimed by UNGA Resolution 68/239.
2. It is organised by UNEP.
3. The World Cities Report 2026 is themed "The Global Housing Crisis: Pathways to Action".
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 2 is wrong: World Cities Day is organised by UN-Habitat.

s:
Consider the following statements in the context of BRICS Sustainable Lifestyle Week (1–7 November 2026):
1. India holds the BRICS Chairmanship in 2026.
2. The first BRIC Summit was held in 2009 at Yekaterinburg.
3. South Africa joined the group in 2011.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 3 is wrong: South Africa joined in 2010.

s: On which date did PM Narendra Modi launch Mission LiFE?
x: Mission LiFE was launched by PM Modi on 20 October 2022.

s: Which of the following pairs (book – author) is correctly matched?
o: The Evolution of TV News in India – Dr. Mercy Jill
The Story of Vande Mataram (Malayalam original) – Harsaran Bir Kaur Pandey
Advantage India: Reshaping the Future for an Equitable World – Ranga Hari
Advantage India: Reshaping the Future for an Equitable World – Anil K. Antony
x: Advantage India is by Anil K. Antony; The Evolution of TV News in India is by Harsaran Bir Kaur Pandey, and The Story of Vande Mataram was written by Ranga Hari and translated by Dr. Mercy Jill.

s: Who released the book "Advantage India: Reshaping the Future for an Equitable World" on 24 October 2026?
x: Vice President C.P. Radhakrishnan released it at the Vice President's Enclave, New Delhi.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The book "The Evolution of TV News in India: From Doordarshan to Digital Disruption" by Harsaran Bir Kaur Pandey is published by Om Books International.
2. Doordarshan began on 15 September 1965.
3. Prasar Bharati was established on 23 November 1997 under the Prasar Bharati Act, 1990.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 2 is wrong: Doordarshan began on 15 September 1959.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The English translation of "The Story of Vande Mataram" was released by Arif Mohammed Khan at the Constitution Club of India, New Delhi.
2. Vande Mataram was adopted as the National Song on 24 January 1950.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: Arif Mohammed Khan released the book on 29 October 2026, and Vande Mataram was adopted as National Song on 24 January 1950.

s: At the Indian National Congress session of which year did Rabindranath Tagore first sing Vande Mataram?
x: Tagore first sang Vande Mataram at the 1896 INC session; it was composed by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay in Anandamath (1882).

s: Which word was named the Collins Dictionary Word of the Year 2026?
x: 'Mogging', slang for outperforming or dominating others, is the Collins Word of the Year 2026; Fire Waves and P(Doom) were other listed terms.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Collins Dictionary Word of the Year 2026:
1. The usage of the chosen word 'Mogging' rose by 210% in 2026.
2. Collins is published by US-based HarperCollins.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 2 is wrong: Collins is published by UK-based HarperCollins.

s: Where did FM Nirmala Sitharaman release the commemorative coin on the 250th birth anniversary of Muthuswami Dikshitar?
x: The coin was released in Varanasi, highlighting Dikshitar's Kashi links.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Muthuswami Dikshitar?
o: The coin released in November 2026 marks his 200th birth anniversary.
x: The coin marks his 250th birth anniversary (he was born in 1775).

s:
Arrange the Carnatic Trinity in chronological order of their birth:
1. Tyagaraja
2. Muthuswami Dikshitar
3. Syama Sastri
x: Syama Sastri (1762), Tyagaraja (1767), Muthuswami Dikshitar (1775).
